entry.title: Information request
entry.content:
We are planning an upgrade of our SAP BW NetWeaver 7.5 system which is currently running on SAP HANA 1.0 SPS12.
Our system landscape is as follows:

• SAP BW 7.5 Application Server running on Windows

• SAP HANA Database running on Linux
While running SAP Maintenance Planner for this system, the target database recommended is SAP HANA Database 2.0 SPS08 (Revision 89) for Linux.
We would like to confirm the following points from SAP:
Whether SAP HANA 2.0 SPS08 Rev. 89 is the correct and supported target version for BW NetWeaver 7.5 when upgrading from HANA 1.0 SPS12.
Whether the mixed OS landscape (Application Server on Windows and HANA Database on Linux) is fully supported for this upgrade scenario.
Whether the upgrade path using SUM with DMO (Database Migration Option) from HANA 1.0 to HANA 2.0 is the recommended and supported approach for this system.
Kindly confirm that the target selected by Maintenance Planner (HANA 2.0 SPS08 Rev. 89 on Linux) is the correct upgrade path for our BW 7.5 system so that we may proceed accordingly.
Your confirmation will help us finalize our upgrade plan.

Our BW system is running with SAP Kernel 7.49. Please confirm that Kernel 7.49 is fully supported for BW 7.5 on SAP HANA 2.0 SPS08, and that there is no conflict between PAM and the relevant SAP Notes for this kernel level.

entry.title: Guidance Needed – Repartitioning HANA Table /BIC/FZIM_C12
entry.content:
We would like your guidance regarding repartitioning one of our large tables in SAP CAR on PERSON_NAME. The table /BIC/FZ***  is currently split into 4 partitions, and we are seeing that partition ID 4 contains approximately 1.7 billion records and is rapidly approaching the 2 billion record limit in PERSON_NAME. Due to this, we are considering repartitioning the table, however we are not sure what the correct partitioning strategy should be.

At present, the table is partitioned using two layers: Round-Robin as the first layer and Range partitioning as the second layer based on the column KEY_*** (ranges 0,1,2). The data distribution appears to be highly skewed, with most records in partition 4 and significantly fewer in the other partitions (partition 1 being the smallest), so we are unsure whether the partitioning was originally done correctly and whether this strategy is appropriate for this table going forward.

We have reviewed SAP Notes such as DIGITS (BW-related) and DIGITS (general PERSON_NAME partitioning recommendations), and we are looking for a recommendation similar to the table-specific guidance mentioned in Question 27 of SAP Note DIGITS where the partition method and column are clearly defined for specific tables.

Could you please advise whether there are any table-specific recommendations for how /BIC/FZ***  should be partitioned, and what partition method and key column(s) would be best to avoid future growth issues?


------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

entry.title: CVSS 9.9 Auth Bypass in SAP BW/BPC — Patch or Mitigate Now (SAP Note 3719353)
entry.content:
Hi All,

Following is the  security disclosure, I’ve summarized the critical vulnerability affecting our SAP landscapes. Unlike standard SQL injections, this is an Authorization Bypass that allows SQL execution through specific upload tools.

Vulnerability Detail: CVE-2026-27681 (SAP Note 3719353)

  • CVSS Score: 9.9 (Critical)
  • Nature of Risk: Authenticated users can bypass authorization checks within specific ABAP upload tools in SAP BPC and BW. This allows for the execution of arbitrary SQL statements, potentially leading to full database compromise (Read/Write/Delete).

Affected Components & Versions:

  • HANABPC: 810
  • BPC4HANA: 300
  • SAP_BW: 750 through 816

Required Action Plan:

  1. Permanent Fix (Priority: High)We need to apply the corrections from SAP Note 3719353 to deactivate the vulnerable code. Please prioritize the following Support Packages for our upcoming maintenance window:
  • SAPK-75035INSAPBW
  • SAPK-81019INHANABPC
  • SAPK-30014INBPC4HANA
  1. Immediate Mitigation (Interim)Until patching is complete, we should immediately restrict the S_GUI authorization object. Specifically, revoking Activity 60 (Upload) from standard end-user roles will block the attack vector by disabling the necessary upload functionality.

Thanks & Regards

HarshaTeja

entry.title: SAP Datasphere: Best Practice for JDBC User Provisioning, Password Management, and Downstream Access
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

We are implementing SAP Datasphere and evaluating a scalable approach for JDBC-based access for multiple downstream applications.

We would appreciate guidance on the following:

  1. JDBC User Provisioning

    • Is there a way to automatically provision a JDBC user from an existing enterprise Functional ID or Service ID?
    • Can JDBC user creation be integrated with a standard identity and access management process, or is manual creation the only option?

  2. Password Management

    • What is the password expiry policy for JDBC users?
    • Can application owners reset JDBC user passwords themselves?
    • Is there a self-service password reset capability available?
    • Can password management be delegated to application owners rather than requiring platform administrators?

  3. Recommended Architecture

    • For multiple downstream consumers, what is the recommended approach?
      • Shared JDBC user across applications?
      • Dedicated JDBC user per application?
      • Service account based approach?
    • Are there SAP-recommended patterns for integrating JDBC credentials with enterprise secrets management solutions and password rotation processes?

Our goal is to establish a secure, scalable, and low-maintenance operational model for SAP Datasphere integrations while minimizing administrative overhead and supporting future growth.

Any best practices, lessons learned, or SAP recommendations would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: BW/4HANA vs Datasphere: how do you debug a missing delta record
entry.content:
How are you troubleshooting data issues in SAP Datasphere without an aDSO-style change log?
In SAP BW/4HANA, the aDSO change log is one of our most-used troubleshooting tools. When a report shows wrong numbers or a delta hasn't loaded properly, we go straight to the change log and can see:

🔹 Which request brought in a record
🔹 The before image and after image of every change
🔹 Exactly when a value changed and what it was before
🔹 Where the gaps are, by comparing requests against the source

In SAP Datasphere, a local table with Delta Capture only keeps the latest version of each record (Change_Type / Change_Date). The internal _Delta table isn't meant for external access, so there's no built-in way to see the old value or trace a change back to a specific load.
For those running Datasphere in production (especially with Replication Flows from S/4HANA):

1️⃣ How do you investigate a missing or wrong delta record today?
2️⃣ Have you built your own change history (append-only history table, SCD Type 2, snapshots)? What worked and what didn't at large volumes?
3️⃣ How do you reconcile Datasphere against the source to spot delta gaps?
